Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Aegis CyberTech Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question queue will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aegis CyberTech's results for the second quarter fiscal 2025. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; and Casey Wong, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Aegis CyberTech continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the second quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about our Aegis XDR platform and the resulting acceleration in multi-product adoptions is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: advancing AI-driven threat detection and response innovations, scaling our cloud-native security offerings including SASE and CSPM, growing our high-value customer base with ARR over $100K, capturing market share through platform differentiation, optimizing average deal sizes via land-and-expand motions, and maintaining disciplined R&D investments while providing clear guidance underpinned by robust assumptions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the second quarter was $348 million, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 92% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 78%, while operating expenses were $240 million. Net income was $45 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.62. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

Let me expand on some key metrics that highlight our momentum. First, on our R&D investment, which is a cornerstone of our competitive edge in an industry where threats evolve faster than ever—think AI-powered polymorphic malware, quantum computing risks to asymmetric encryption, and ransomware-as-a-service platforms like LockBit 3.0. Maintaining a robust R&D cadence is existential for leadership in next-gen solutions like our Nebula XDR and Zero-Trust Edge suites. For the quarter, we deployed 18.4% of revenue into R&D, up 120 basis points sequentially and 210 basis points year-over-year, equating to about $64 million on our quarterly revenue. Full-year fiscal 2023 saw us at 17.9% or $492 million against $2.75 billion in revenue, a 90 basis point increase from the prior year. This positions us competitively—high-end like Palo Alto at 18-20% or CrowdStrike at 22-24%, ahead of legacy players at 12-15% who struggle with zero-days like Log4Shell derivatives or MOVEit attacks.

Our trend has ticked up steadily: 15.2% in FY2021, 17.0% in FY2022, now 17.9% in FY2023, tied to our Threat Horizon framework allocating across near-term (60%), mid-term (25%), and long-term (15%) efforts. Near-term drove 40% growth in Nebula XDR subscriptions with generative AI for threat hunting, detecting lateral movement three times faster and slashing MTTD from hours to minutes. Mid-term, $85 million into SASE convergence integrating SWG, ZTNA, and CASB to rival Cato and Netskope. Regionally, North America got 65% for cloud-native security amid 300% multi-cloud breach surges per Mandiant; EMEA 20% or $98 million for GDPR/DORA tools with NLP data classification; APAC 12% or $59 million countering Lazarus Group with IoT/OT honeypots; and emerging LATAM via telco 5G stacks.

Strategically, this builds our moat—142 patents filed last year on post-quantum crypto like Kyber partnering with NIST and IBM, 22% R&D team growth poaching from DARPA and FAANG, plus the $200 million QuantumSafe Labs acquisition for CRYSTALS-Dilithium in VPNs. Looking ahead, FY2024 R&D guides to 18-19% or $650-700 million on $3.6 billion revenue, funding Nebula AI Phase 2 with federated learning and sovereign clouds for finance/healthcare, where we top MITRE ATT&CK evals. This isn't a cost; it's our advantage against Clop ransomware—we anticipate threats.

Shifting to our customer momentum, a key leading indicator is customers with over $100K ARR. We ended Q2 with 478 such customers, up 36% year-over-year from 352 and 11% sequentially from 431 in Q1. They represent 68% of our $1.42 billion total ARR base, up from 62% last year, powering our revenue beat. Over 75% of new expansions—94 customers—came from upsells via our Unified Threat Platform, bundling Aegis XDR with CWP and SASE. A U.S. financial firm expanded from $45K EDR pilot to $250K full-stack with GenAI behavioral analytics against deepfakes, aligning with IDC's 60% multi-product spend shift.

Regionally balanced: North America 312 customers (65%), +32% YoY with 15 Fortune 100 including hyperscalers; EMEA 105, +52% on GDPR/Clop MOVEit-driven DLP/ZTNA; APAC 61, +41% via Tokyo DC and NTT amid Sophos' 300% ransomware spike; LatAm near 30 in Brazil PIX threats. Our ML threat hunting on 15 trillion signals daily improves MTTD 40%, with 68% adopting Autonomous SOC automating 85% triage via graph engines—98% retention, 112% gross retention. Targeting 550+ by FY2025 end via channels like Deloitte/Accenture (45% Q2 wins), vertical playbooks for HIPAA/OT, and CSPM acquisition integrations.

On market share trends, IDC data shows us expanding EDR share from 8.2% H1 2022 to 11.7% H2 2023, +350 bps, fastest Leader in Gartner's Magic Quadrant climbing from Challenger. CSPM at 14.3% up from 10.9%, eroding Prisma/Zscaler with CNAPP and 40% fewer false positives via NexusAI. SASE +220 bps to 9.8% beating Cisco Umbrella with NexusOne console, 62% faster MTTR per AV-TEST; MDR +280 bps to 8.9%, 98.7% MITRE catch topping Falcon by 12 points amid 3.5M job shortages.

North America 18.4% enterprise EDR share via AWS/Azure; EMEA doubled to 7.2% with PQC ahead of NIST for Deutsche Bank/BNP; APAC 4.1% to 6.8% in keiretsu/APT41 via Tokyo DC; LatAm +45% YoY to 2.3%. NexusAI 2.0 on 15PB telemetry preempts deepfakes (+300% per Proofpoint), NPS +28% to 72, 142% top-100 expansion; ThreatZero M&A boosts ITDR 22% vs Okta. Sustaining 200-300 bps gains via GenAI NexusShield and OT/IoT.

Average deal size also reflects GTM strength—Q4 overall $285K ACV, +28% YoY from $222K, via multi-module bundles of FalconXDR, SASE, CSPM. New logos $312K +42% YoY, 65% over $500K TCV in Fortune 500 against Change Healthcare ransomware; expansions $248K +19%, 128% NBR, 40% SASE upgrades, 17 $1M+ deals. FY2023 +32% to $267K, new $295K +38%, expansions $235K +27%, outpacing peers.

North America $310K new logos on CISA zero-trust; EMEA $265K +45% NIS2/Conti; APJ $240K +52% Essential Eight/SolarWinds. CyberShield Fusion Kubernetes deployment cuts TTV to 30 days, 70% SIEM attach, 12% mega-deals >$5M TCV. FY2024 +25-30% with PQC/SCRM post-MOVEit, 95% retention in $75B TAM.

Now, turning to next quarter billings guidance, our leading indicator for subscription revenue. Q2 billings $278 million beat high-end $265-275M guidance, +37% YoY, on 128% dollar net retention from multi-product expansions in Next-Gen XDR and CSPM. Top 500 customers averaged $2.5M+ ACV enterprise deals, +22% YoY, consolidating on SASE/Zero Trust.

For Q3, guiding $295-310 million, 34-42% YoY at $302.5M midpoint, factoring sales ramp/seasonality. Product drivers 65% upside: XDR/AI +55% QoQ, $45-50M Q3 on Agentic AI GA reducing MTTR 70% in ransomware sims, 15 Fortune 100 wins; Cloud SASE/CSPM 40% net new ACV, AWS Marketplace/FedRAMP unlocking $20M public sector; Quantum-Resistant Encryption $10M tailwind, 80% pilot conversion vs APT41.

Regions: NA 65% +38% YoY post-CrowdStrike outage favoring multi-cloud/agentless, three hyperscaler wins; EMEA 20% +50% NIS2/DACH Deutsche Telekom/London DC $25M; APAC 15% +25% Japan NTT offsetting FX, China <5%. Market resilient IDC 14.3% to $212B 2025, we +35% land-expand; ransomware +30% Chainalysis, CISO budgets +18%, 95% retention, 70% three+ modules vs Palo Alto.

Risks: sales cycles 105 days +13, federal delays 10% pipeline, but $1.2B RPO +45% YoY 2.8x coverage. Raising FY2025 billings $1.15-1.18B +36%, revenue $1.05-1.07B, 25%+ margins FY2026 35% CAC payback.

Finally, assumptions for FY25 guidance: revenue $1.25-1.35B +22-30%, ARR $1.1-1.2B +25-33%, op margin 28-30%. Pillars: market 13.8% CAGR Gartner, ransomware +37% Chainalysis $2M payouts, SASE $15B 2027 IDC, breaches $4.88M IBM, recession-proof.

Customer: NRR 118-120%, top 500 125%+ 90-day, 350-400 new logos 28% $450M pipeline close, <3% churn 38-month contracts, $250M RPO 92%. Product: Nexus AI Sentinel 35% inc ARR 40% faster MTTR vs Falcon/Defender pilots, OT/IoT 20% attach Siemens $10B TAM, 85% multi-product +7pp.

Regions: Americas 62% +24% CISA/AWS Bedrock +45% QoQ; EMEA 24% +28% NIS2 €2.7B fines DLP Deutsche; APAC 14% +35% NTT/Reliance SASE. Ops: sales 0.85x 32% rev, R&D 18% 12 modules PQC, FCF 30% DSO 65 capex <3%, FX neutral, 2 M&A <$200M SCRM/SBOM 15%. Risks AI threats/budgets, buffer 65 Rule 40. Conservative on 95% margins 1.8x retention $225B market.

Thank you. Now over to Taylor.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities, particularly in areas like generative AI for autonomous response in XDR, cloud-native protections with low false positives, and emerging quantum-resistant technologies to stay ahead of nation-state threats.

Morgan Patel: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape—from ransomware surges to supply chain vulnerabilities like Log4Shell—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure with zero-trust principles and advanced behavioral analytics.

Casey Wong: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals, from North America enterprises to EMEA compliance drivers and APAC growth markets. Our sales team is executing well, closing larger deals through channel partnerships with firms like Deloitte, Accenture, and telcos such as NTT and Deutsche Telekom to reach a wider audience.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for participating in the question and answer session: Press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen: Thanks. Jordan, great quarter on billings. Can you elaborate more on the Q3 drivers, especially the AI XDR ramp and any regional risks?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. As I detailed, the $45-50 million from XDR stems from Agentic AI GA and Fortune 100 design wins slashing MTTR 70%. NA post-outage momentum, EMEA NIS2, APAC NTT offset FX—risks like cycles are visibility-covered by RPO.

Operator: Next question from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel: Hi team. On the $100K+ ARR customers, how sustainable is the 36% growth, and what's the mix shift?

Alex Rivera: Lisa, thanks. That 478 cohort, 68% of ARR, grows via proven land-expand—upsells bundling XDR/SASE/CWP, regional balance NA/EMEA/APAC, Autonomous SOC stickiness at 98% retention. Targeting 550+ sustainably through channels and verticals.

Operator: Next question from Raj Singh with Barclays.

Raj Singh: Taylor, curious on R&D specifics—how does 18%+ intensity translate to tech edges versus peers?

Taylor Kim: Raj, spot on. Our allocation fuels near-term AI hunting three times faster MTTD, mid SASE integrations, long PQC patents with NIST—outpacing on MITRE, federated learning privacy, OT honeypots, ahead of polymorphic/AI threats where peers lag.

Operator: Next question from Emily Torres with JPMorgan.

Emily Torres: Thanks. Market share gains impressive—thoughts on competitive positioning in SASE/CSPM, and deal size trends?

Morgan Patel: Emily, our 11.7% EDR, 14.3% CSPM shares via NexusAI low falses, SASE 9.8% single-console MTTR edge beat Umbrella. Deal sizes $285K avg +28%, new $312K enterprises bundling against ransomware, FY +25-30% mega-deals PQC/SCRM.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
